By Francisco Rodrigues | Edited by Aoyon Ashraf Oct 25, 2026, 11:00 a.m. EDT 3 min read Make preferred on Share Share this article Copy link X icon X (Twitter) LinkedIn Facebook Email Make preferred on Summary Show Latvia could have rules for tokenizing real-world assets in the first half of 2027, with commercial property a possible start, its economics minister said. Government bonds are on the “priority list” and could be tokenized in the first part of next year, Viktors Valainis said, without giving issuance details. A legal assessment due Oct. 1 is “still ongoing,” and Valainis’s party won no seats in this month’s election as Latvia forms a new government. By Jamie Crawley , AI Boost | Edited by Sheldon Reback Oct 25, 2026, 9:00 a.m. EDT 3 min read Make preferred on Share Share this article Copy link X icon X (Twitter) LinkedIn Facebook Email Make preferred on Canary Wharf, London (Pixabay) Summary Show More than 10,000 complaints about bank restrictions on cryptocurrency transactions were submitted across the U.K. during a 90-day period, according to the advocacy group Stand With Crypto. Lloyds Banking Group received the most complaints, followed by Barclays and NatWest, though the voluntary data was not adjusted for each bank’s market share and does not represent all customers. Stand With Crypto said banks’ blanket bans, rigid limits and unclear policies could impede access to regulated exchanges and undermine Britain’s ambition to become a global cryptocurrency hub.
